name: albanian_01
context: A Facebook comment under a post by the National Institute of Public Health of Kosovo during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The comment is in Albanian, mostly the informal Kosovo (Gheg) dialect, often written without the letters ë and ç.

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 0 sends far too many neutral texts to negative. The annotators use neutral as the default for complaints about citizens, lockdown demands, skeptical questions, forecasts, politics and league-style jokes. Negative needs explicit hostility: lying accusations, insults, vulgar curses, scornful mockery or despair. Positive centres on thanks, praise and blessings, even when mixed with criticism. Bare hopes and cheering stay neutral. This version is trimmed to stay under 400 words.

Version 1 fixed neutral (295 of 329 right) but overcorrected: negative recall fell to 78 of 173. Missed negatives fall into five groups: blame on the government, ministers or parties ('Qeveria koti ika fajet', 'fajtor shteti'); insults to citizens ('injoranta', 'palaqo', 'pa morrun vesh'); vulgar curses ('nanen ja qifsha'); sarcastic doubt or mockery of the Institute's numbers, errors or delays ('e kan gabu', 'diqka qitu spo shkon', 'testet me sy'); and alarm ('bomb atomice', 'ma keq', 'e hupet kontrollen'). Sarcastic praise ('Mashalla ... gjdo dite ma shum raste', 'krenar me ty') is also negative. Positive lost texts showing relief at falling numbers or recoveries and shared encouragement, so those go back to positive. False positives include a thanks attached to a plain question or request, which is neutral, plus league jokes and tags. Neutral remains plain complaints about mask-wearing without insult, neutral questions, lockdown suggestions, forecasts and banter.

Version 2 swung back: 139 neutral texts went to negative, because 'sarcastic doubt' and 'alarm' covered most skeptical or worried comments, which annotators call neutral. Examples are 'testu me sy' (tested by eye), number discrepancies, 'two weeks are critical', and complaints about citizens without insult. Version 1, with neutral as the default, scored best. Keep that base and add only explicit negative triggers: vulgar curses, insult words aimed at people or officials, explicit blame words aimed at the government ('fajet', 'fajtor', 'deshtim'), lying claims, direct contempt for the Institute ('unlike faqes', 'si Odeoni'), and sarcastic praise of the government. Skeptical questions, discrepancies, forecasts, worry and mask complaints stay neutral. Positive also covers clear relief at falling numbers or recoveries, but not city-league cheering. A thanks that only prefaces a question stays neutral.

Version 3 is the best so far (73.9). The largest remaining loss is 56 negatives labelled neutral. Many are short cries of horror or despair ('tmer', 'Tmerrshem', 'Katastrof', 'Ma za ma keq per ne', 'Prishtina si bomb atomice'), so explicit horror and despair words become negative triggers. Others ridicule the Institute's competence ('ju ka hup topi' (you've lost the plot), 'e kan gabu' (they got it wrong), 'koka punsu ne laborator'), so mocking the Institute for errors joins as a trigger. Plain questions about discrepancies stay neutral. Missed insults ('palaqo', 'bosa', 'huti') and blame of the new government without the word 'fajet' ('Prej qe u formu qeveria e re...') are also added. False positives are mainly city-league cheering, tags, ads and bare 'it's almost over' remarks, which are now named as neutral. The neutral-default structure is kept to protect the gains.

Version 4 (75.0) improved negative recall, but neutral-to-negative rose to 52. Many of those are laughing banter about cities, testing or tagged friends ('Mirupafshim ne Shtator... ra pi liges', 'breshka snxan', 'copy paste postimin me 0 raste'), jokes about citizens, and political remarks not aimed at the current authorities. The fix is to state that humor and banter stay neutral unless they contain a lying claim, a curse, or direct contempt for the Institute or government. Several clear negatives were missed because lying claims came in variant spellings ('ona mytet tu na rrejt', 'hajde ren hajde'), so those spellings go into the cues. Neutral-to-positive errors are tags or names that look like words ('Urim', 'Drbest'), off-topic chat, ads, city cheering and suggestions ('Postoni mire'). Positive now needs an expressed approving feeling, not just a mention of numbers. The rest of the structure stays.

Version 5 is the best so far (77.8). The clearest fixable errors are positives sent to negative even though they contain explicit thanks or praise: 'Instituti flm...', '...e juve instiut ju lumte per punen', 'bravo ju koft veq vazhdoni' and 'ka qen Minister shembull'. The model treats the angry or ironic surrounding text as decisive or reads 'bravo' as sarcasm. Annotators count such praise as positive, so the override is made explicit: sincere thanks or praise toward the Institute, health staff or a person wins over criticism of citizens or the government. 'Bravo' and 'ju lumt' count as sarcasm only when they praise worsening results. Short approvals ('mire' (good), 'Supper', 'keni perparu' (you've improved)) also go into the positive cues. Harsh complaints about careless citizens without an insult word, and remarks about past politicians, are again stated as neutral, to reduce neutral-to-negative errors. The rest is unchanged.

Version 6 raised positive recall, but neutral-to-positive grew. The causes were the generic cue 'mire' (good), which caught suggestions, and the dropped 'ma gjall' neutral example, after which city cheering went to positive. This version goes back to version 5, the best so far. It keeps the 'ma gjall' neutral example, drops the generic 'mire' and 'super' cues, and keeps a lighter form of the praise override: explicit thanks or praise to someone beats surrounding criticism. City cheering, tags, ads and suggestions are stated as neutral. The rule is trimmed to stay under 400 words.

Versions 5 to 7 vary by only about 2 points, and versions 6 and 7 lost precision when the praise override was strengthened, so this version goes back to version 5's wording, the best so far (77.8). Two errors persist in every version. First, jokes with exaggerated comparisons ('Rastet Jane ne Hiroshima', 'breshka snxan', 'copy paste postimin me 0 raste', 'kem me kalu kinen') are sent to negative when annotators mark them neutral. Second, policy complaints that criticise government decisions without blaming or insulting anyone ('qeverija si mban fjalet', 'Tani dojn mi hjek masat') are also called neutral by annotators. Both are now stated explicitly as neutral, while explicit blame of the current government ('fajet', 'Qeveria Koti') stays negative. The other wording is trimmed to stay within the limit.

Versions 5 to 8 sit on a plateau of 76 to 78, and the differences are mostly run noise and trade-offs. Every extra emphasis either moves neutral texts into positive (a stronger praise override, cheering) or leaves the neutral and negative balance unchanged (the policy-complaint wording in version 8). Version 8 also dropped the 'Mirupafshim ne Shtator... ra pi liges' neutral example, and that text went back to negative. So version 9 restores version 5's wording and examples, the best so far at 77.8, with only small additions. It adds 'bomb' and 'Qeveria Koti' (the Kurti government) as negative cues, because texts like 'Prishtina si bomb atomice' and 'Qeveria Koti' blame were missed. It keeps exaggerated comparisons and policy complaints without blame words in the neutral rule, compactly. Long explanations stay out to keep the model's decision boundary stable.

This is the final version. Versions 5 to 9 all score between 76 and 78. The remaining errors are mostly annotator inconsistency: near-identical texts get different gold labels, as with skeptical number remarks, city jokes and harsh complaints about citizens. Further wording changes have only traded errors between classes. Version 9, which was version 5 plus a few cues and rule phrases, scored 76.6, so those additions did not help. The safest choice is to return version 5 essentially unchanged, since it had the best measured balance (77.8). It keeps neutral as the default, explicit negative triggers (curses, insults, government blame, lying claims in any spelling, ridicule of the Institute, sarcastic praise, horror words), and positive for expressed approval, with the laughing-banter, city-cheering and tag exclusions.
